steps: Title globe, tapped Ceasefire or Collapse, chose Ukraine
Played all 12 months, mostly approving the cabinet pick
Reached verdict, moments, truth and ranking screens
scenarios.notes: Right leaders and a real-world comparison, but the ceasefire arc was replaced by generic template crises (strike, cyberattack, scandal) and the war simply ended in month 6 with no terms or negotiation.

steps: Read the Hurts/Helps tags and staff reasons each month

suggestions.what: Make the Ukraine flashpoint crises about the talks: territory, security guarantees, coalition of the willing, sanctions, with a visible negotiation track
When a war ends, say why in the paper and result card
Reaction quotes should name the real actor and issue, not a template
Make the verdict grade follow progress (ceasefire counts), and fix the Better than 0% line
Bring The truth comparison forward, even as an optional hint during play

delight: The truth screen with ISW and Abu Dhabi context and sources (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-01/shots/priya-tablet/047-truth.png)
Staff reasons and Hurts/Helps tags on each card (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-01/shots/priya-tablet/007-desk.png)

fun.reason: Smooth and handsome, but after month 2 I was approving picks.

clarity.reason: Cards explain intent well; score scales and green drops confuse.

visual.reason: Scenes, stamps and paper look crafted on tablet.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Choices are real but the world felt scripted by templates.

agency.reason: Never blocked; but the war ended without my doing.

realism.reason: Leaders right, but crises generic, a midterm error, a template quote.

replay.reason: I would try Russia or the US seat for the truth screen.

recommend.reason: I would recommend it to a Model UN friend for the debrief, with caveats about the middle.

verbatim: The end screen taught me something. The middle months felt like any country's generic crises, not Ukraine in November 2026.
